📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has already instituted a major change at Manchester United in a bid to lift the club’s standards and dodge relegation.

The Argentine’s United tenure got off to a grim start at Anfield on Sunday as Leny Yoro was shown an early red card and Liverpool went on to bag four goals.

The result leaves the club 19th in the Premier League, with the prospect of relegation - or, at the very least, being involved in the relegation battle - more real than ever.

But as Pochettino discovers the true scale of the task at hand, he has wasted little time in imposing his methods on United.

That has begun with scrapping a rule imposed by his predecessor Michael Carrick, who was sacked during the November international break.

While in the job, Carrick had habitually handed the United squad a day off following a match, but Pochettino has promptly done away with that provision.

His players reported to Carrington bright and early on Monday morning for recovery sessions, with a Champions League meeting with Sporting looming on Wednesday evening.

Pochettino has pushed forward their arrival time, too, with some players touching down at the training ground as early as 8.30am.

According to recent reports, it has been a busy few days at Carrington. Pochettino has hired a fresh strength and conditioning coach to help accommodate his focus on high-pressing football, while the club are also appealing Yoro’s red card.

They are doing so on the basis that Senne Lammens looked set to beat Alexander Isak in his footrace, and, thus, Yoro’s clumsy tackle did not constitute denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

Reacting to the penalty decision post-match, Pochettino noted: “It's not ok to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after [eight] minutes. Now we can explain everything but the damage is done, it's so painful.

"The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak.

“When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper, he runs and goes down.

Sources indicate that "In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal, everyone who plays football can feel it.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 12:44.
  • Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee could reportedly become the first player to leave Old Trafford during the January transfer window.
  • The Dutchman joined the Red Devils from Bologna in the summer of 2024 and has since made 86 appearances for the club across all competitions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 23 Nov 2026 12:44.

Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee could reportedly become the first player to leave Old Trafford during the January transfer window.

The Dutchman joined the Red Devils from Bologna in the summer of 2024 and has since made 86 appearances for the club across all competitions.

Zirkzee has managed just 11 goals and four assists for Man Utd and was heavily linked with a move away from the club during the summer transfer window.

Several Serie A clubs were keen to sign him, with Fiorentina reportedly agreeing a loan fee for the striker, but the proposed move ultimately failed to materialise.

Premier League rivals Everton also made a late push for the 25-year-old, but Man Utd were unwilling to let him leave without first securing a replacement.

Former Man Utd manager Michael Carrick even suggested that Zirkzee could become an vital player for the club, but the striker has since slipped considerably down the pecking order.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport (via Manchester Evening News), Zirkzee is expected to become the first player to depart in January, with several Italian clubs competing for his signature.

Juventus and Fiorentina are reportedly keen to sign the striker, while Napoli could also enter the race.

The former Bayern Munich attacker has made just seven substitute appearances in the Premier League this season, accumulating 134 minutes of action and scoring once.

Zirkzee has also featured three times as a substitute in the Champions League, where he has registered another goal.

Mauricio Pochettino introduced him in the second half of Man Utd's 4-0 defeat against Liverpool, and the Dutchman managed to make a positive impression despite the disappointing result.

Towards the end of the contest, Zirkzee produced a brilliant pass to Bruno Fernandes, but the United captain's effort was comfortably saved by Alisson Becker.

If Zirkzee fails to earn more opportunities under Pochettino over the coming month, the likelihood of him leaving Old Trafford could increase considerably.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believes a red card for Leny Yoro during Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat by Liverpool was the correct decision - claiming it “would’ve been a surprise” if the defender wasn’t sent off.
  • Man Utd informed the Football Association (FA) on Monday afternoon of their intention to appeal Yoro’s three-game suspension.
  • After just eight minutes of Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge of United at Anfield, Yoro found himself scrambling to get back after Matthijs de Ligt allowed Alexander Isak through on goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believes a red card for Leny Yoro during Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat by Liverpool was the correct decision - claiming it “would’ve been a surprise” if the defender wasn’t sent off.

Man Utd informed the Football Association (FA) on Monday afternoon of their intention to appeal Yoro’s three-game suspension.

After just eight minutes of Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge of United at Anfield, Yoro found himself scrambling to get back after Matthijs de Ligt allowed Alexander Isak through on goal.

Chasing both man and ball, Yoro clipped Isak on the edge of the area - prompting referee Sam Barrott to show a straight red card. At the time Pochettino was spotted aggressively waving his finger, clearly disagreeing with the decision.

But on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch panel, Gallagher couldn’t see any mitigating factors for Yoro.

Recent findings suggest that he said: “If you look at it from the referee's angle, is it a foul? That's the first step. Yeah. Is he in possession of the ball? From that angle, yes.

“I think most people would've expected a red card. It would've been a surprise during the game if a red card hadn't been given.”.

United fans pointed out that goalkeeper Senne Lammens appeared to be reaching the loose ball before Isak, potentially changing the foul from a denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

Sources indicate that asked if he thought that Lammens would have gotten to the ball first, Gallagher replied: "I don't know. You watch it play out. That happens. Do you think it's a red card? Gary Neville's immediate reaction was red card.”.

Recent findings suggest that gallagher’s fellow pundit, former England striker Jay Bothroyd, was in agreement. "It has to be a red,” he mentioned.

“I will say, I'm not sure Isak can get a shot off, but I think he could touch the ball. It's not an obvious goalscoring opportunity, but you don't know. You have to judge if it's a foul, so you have to give the red card.

In a recent development, “Technically, he is in control of the ball because he touched it in that direction. It's if he's heavy or not.".

Sources indicate that ex-Tottenham manager Tim Sherwood was less certain. He stated: "I think if he hadn't been given a red he could've gotten away with it by saying Isak wasn't in control of the ball. I think I can listen to both sides.

Sources indicate that "You have to assess where Lammens was. The ball was nearly in his hands.".

There was further frustration for United on Merseyside, with Pochettino believing that his side should have been awarded a penalty in the first half.

Bryan Mbeumo found himself barged off the ball by Jeremy Jacquet inside the box, but the entire panel rejected those claims.

Industry observers note that gallagher explained: “When players are side by side, you can do that. They are side by side. Jacquet was even in front of him.".

Sources indicate that bothroyd concurred: "If I am Pochettino, I am telling Mbeumo to get in the gym. That is just strength.".

Sherwood agreed, admiring Jacquet. He concluded: "No penalty. How good is he by the way, Jacquet?".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:24 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 16:32 EST, 19 November 2026.

Blackpool have sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy birthday.

Recent findings suggest that evatt had been in charge for a year and his final match was Saturday's 1-0 away defeat by fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, when his squad was decimated by illness. The result left the Seasiders immediately above the League One relegation zone and followed a run of one win and six defeats in ten league games.

Blackpool’s social media team had earlier wished Evatt a happy 45th birthday with the pay-off line: 'Have a great day, Gaffer!'.

Three hours later, Evatt was relieved of his duties, and the club began the search for their ninth manager in eight years.

In a recent development, evatt’s contract was set to run until June 2028. He joined last October following his exit from Bolton Wanderers in January 2025.

Blackpool later thanked the 45-year-old for his efforts during his time with the club.

Blackpool sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy 45th birthday.

Blackpool posted the birthday message just after 9am in the morning, with Evatt's sacking then confirmed at 4pm.

Former Crystal Palace chairman Simon Jordan famously claimed to have sacked Trevor Francis on his birthday back in 2003.

Francis' dismissal has become an often told tale, with Jordan writing sixteen years after the event that he had even offered to send the former England star a birthday card.

Recent reports have also involved the suggestion that Francis had mumbled 'but its my birthday' back to Jordan when he was given his marching orders.

Industry observers note that whether these events played out as told are unclear. But Crystal Palace officially confirmed Francis' departure on April 18 in 2003, with his birthday falling a day later.

'I am totally committed to playing in the Premier League and I will ensure the new manager can achieve this aspiration,' Jordan wrote on Crystal Palace's website at the time. 'I would like to thank Trevor for all his hard work and would like to wish him the very best for the future.'.

Industry observers note that jordan then turned on the players, adding: 'I'm not watching next year what I've had to watch this year. At times we've been a disgrace.

Industry observers note that 'I've asked the management staff to tell me who should go. They can see the players who are performing and those who are not and you will see in the summer, out they will go. The players will be told when it suits me. I care about them as much they care about me.'.

Francis had reportedly told his players in a parting shot: 'Well, lads, I've been sacked – have a good summer holiday.'.

Palace appointed Steve Kember as manager in the summer and despite Jordan's hopes of automatic promotion, rather than the play-offs, found themselves in a relegation battle in November.

Iain Dowie was appointed as manager the following month and guided Palace into the play-offs, with the Eagles triumphing in Cardiff to secure promotion to the top flight.

Steve Thompson will step in to take charge of the team against Wigan Athletic this weekend, his fourth spell as caretaker, alongside Stephen Crainey, Stephen Dobbie and Steve Banks.

According to recent reports, during a hugely successful playing career at Bloomfield Road, Evatt made over 250 appearances for Blackpool. In his six years at the club, he played a vital role in their rise from League One to the Premier League, which included two successful play-off campaigns.

On arrival as a manager, he amassed 13 points from a possible 15 in December 2025 to lift them out of the relegation zone, although they lost ten and won two of their next 15 matches in all competitions.

They finished the campaign strongly, with six wins in seven games as part of a sequence of one defeat in 13 between mid-March and the end of August, only to struggle again this season.

Luca Williams-Barnett revealed that Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi played a prank on the teenager ahead of his maiden Premier League goal for the club.

The 18-year-old grabbed the opener against Ipswich Town at the weekend, before going on to mark his first full Premier League start with an assist for Dominic Solanke.

The winger had been involved in the first-team squad for the last four Premier League games prior to the Ipswich match, and had continued to train with De Zerbi’s squad in the week.

As such, being told that he was playing for the Under-21s would have been a shock for the young star.

He revealed De Zerbi’s practical joke in an interview with SpursPlay: "The day before, the gaffer obviously pulled me aside.

According to recent reports, "He actually stated, ‘You’re going to be playing with the ‘21s, 60 minutes to get your legs back,’ and I was like, ‘What?’ but obviously he told me the news and the whole day I was just buzzing. I couldn’t wait.

"Everything I’ve dreamed of. Obviously scoring and getting an assist, it’s like a dream come true basically.".

Williams-Barnett admitted he thought he had spurned his chance for a dream debut, missing a similar opportunity to the move that led to his goal.

He mentioned: “The first ball into the box I wasn’t really there and I was quite annoyed because it was open and I could have had the goal.

It has been revealed that “Once I saw it go back to Pedro [Porro], it was an instinct. Once I saw he was able to cross the ball, I just had to get behind my man and put the ball in the goal.”.

Mikel Arteta has effectively confirmed that Kepa Arrizabalaga will start in goal for Arsenal in the absence of David Raya.

The Gunners will be without first-choice stopper Raya on Tuesday night for the Champions League match at home to Borussia Dortmund.

Sources indicate that the Spaniard was forced off late on against Newcastle at the weekend with a shoulder injury. While that has not proved to be a serious issue and Arsenal have been encouraged by the results of early scans, the Dortmund match will come too soon.

Arteta has split minutes in the Carabao Cup this season between back-up goalkeepers Kepa and Illan Meslier, but it is Kepa who has been on the bench throughout the Premier League season and he came on for Raya against Newcastle.

Discussing his options to replace Raya on Monday, Arteta indicated that Kepa is expected to serve as deputy.

“I think it’s clear for us who is going to play tomorrow,” the Arsenal boss said at his pre-Dortmund press conference.

Kepa started the Carabao Cup third round win over Ipswich earlier this season, but summer signing Meslier then got the nod in the shock last-16 defeat at fourth-tier Fleetwood.

That was despite Kepa being fit and in the matchday squad. However, that was due to a desire to reward Meslier with an opportunity, rather than the Frenchman taking the No2 spot from Kepa.

“Because I want everybody to be part of it,” Arteta noted, explaining the decision to start Meslier against Fleetwood.

“To feel part of it, you need to play. Illan has been really good with us. We believed that it was the right thing to share those minutes in the competition.

“To give a player that every single day is so consistent, so reliable, so supportive with the rest of the boys, to give the feeling that we trust him as well.”.

Arteta was coy on whether Raya will be available on Sunday when leaders Arsenal host Manchester City in the Premier League.

The Spaniard is set for further tests to determine an exact timeframe for his return but any absence would be a huge blow for the Gunners.

Raya kept seven clean sheets in the first 11 league matches of the season and is firm favourite to win a fourth consecutive Golden Glove award, assuming he does not face an extended spell out.

“We have seen what David brings to the team but as well that is why we are very protected with Kepa and Illan,” Arteta noted.

“Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen and now we need to show everyone how well we are protected and the good keepers that we have with Kepa and Illan.”.

Raya is key to Arsenal not just as a shot-stopper but in terms of the team’s build-up play too, with his confidence on the ball both playing short and over the press.

Asked whether Arsenal would have to play differently without him, Arteta mentioned: “We adapt to players’ qualities, they all have different ones.

“There are certain things in our game or in the way that we understand and want to play the game, everybody has to be 100 per cent committed to do.

“But then we make adjustments in relation to the qualities of the players.”.

Real Madrid: Mourinho faces attacking dilemma ahead of Champions League clash with PSV

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1106 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 13:19.
  • Real Madrid go into Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV on the back of nine consecutive victories, but with important concerns for Jose Mourinho to manage.
  • Vinicius Junior came off the bench to take a direct part in both goals, with the assist for Carlos Espi deciding the match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 13:19.

Real Madrid go into Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV on the back of nine consecutive victories, but with important concerns for Jose Mourinho to manage. Saturday's 2-1 comeback win over Celta Vigo was another example of the team's ability to react, but it also exposed problems that the manager cannot ignore.

Vinicius Junior came off the bench to take a direct part in both goals, with the assist for Carlos Espi deciding the match. The Brazilian, who had served a four-match suspension in La Liga, has regained prominence and has already had his place in the starting line-up for the European tie confirmed by Mourinho. At the same time, the Spanish centre-forward again showed that he can be decisive even with few minutes on the pitch.

The challenge is to find room for so many options without compromising the collective structure. Real Madrid have Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius, Jude Bellingham, Arda Guler, Yan Diomande and Espi, as well as names who could come into the mix, such as Endrick and Bernardo Silva, but they cannot simply put them all on the pitch and hope that individual talent solves everything.

Industry observers note that vinicius's display against Celta was a reminder of what the Brazilian offers Real Madrid. Coming on 12 minutes into the second half, he gave the attack depth and was able to unbalance defenders in one-on-one situations. For the equaliser, he started the move that ended with Bellingham. For the winner, he crossed for Espi to pounce on the rebound.

It has been revealed that mourinho confirmed that the Brazilian will start against PSV, ending the debate about his status in the team. Peter Bosz's side are known for high pressing, aggressive defending and their attempts to win the ball back swiftly. When that first press is beaten, however, they tend to offer space behind the defenders.

According to recent reports, that is precisely where Vinicius can be decisive. With his acceleration and ability to attack the space in behind, the Brazilian is a constant threat to a defence that often plays a high line and takes on individual duels all over the pitch. Mbappe can also exploit these spaces.

In a recent development, the question for Mourinho is how to make this threat work without leaving the midfield exposed. Real Madrid cannot rely solely on winning the ball back and launching it to the forwards. They need players close by to connect transitions and sustain possession when necessary.

Industry observers note that the presence of Bellingham and Guler between the lines could be important. The Englishman offers ball-carrying and arrivals into the box, while the Turkey international has the quality to find passes that speed up the attack. But the team needs a solid base behind them. Without that, the freedom of the attacking players could prove costly.

Espi's situation is another dilemma. The 21-year-old forward scored the winner against Celta and has three goals in only 44 minutes played in La Liga this season. It is impressive efficiency, but it does not necessarily mean that he should start.

Mourinho was clear in explaining the Spaniard's characteristics. Espi is a penalty-box centre-forward, strong in the air, able to play with his back to goal and to attack the spaces close to the six-yard box. He is not, however, a forward with great mobility to take part constantly in build-up play. The manager also mentioned that the squad does not have the right characteristics to play a pure 4-4-2 with Mbappe and Espi together.

Sources indicate that mbappe likes to start from the left or occupy the space between the full-back and the centre-back, but he is not a traditional winger who tracks the opposition full-back back into his own half. Vinicius also needs freedom to receive the ball wide and accelerate. Putting Espi alongside the Frenchman would require the two wide players to tuck in more and help form a four-man midfield line.

There are alternatives, but all involve compromises. Bellingham could play deeper, for example. The problem is that Real Madrid would lose part of the Englishman's ability to arrive in the box and would need a midfielder with greater defensive responsibility to compensate. It would also be possible to use Espi in matches where the opposition sit deep and offer less space for the runs of Vinicius and Mbappe.

Recent findings suggest that against tired defences and crosses, Espi offers something different from the other forwards in the squad. His efficiency as a substitute should not be confused with an obligation to change the whole structure of the team.

The win over Celta also left a warning. After turning the scoreline around, Real Madrid finished the game with four forwards on the pitch, as well as Bellingham and Guler in midfield. Mourinho admitted that the team became unbalanced and that he would have liked an extra substitution to bring on Tchouameni and restore defensive protection.

Recent findings suggest that under Bosz, PSV rely on high pressing, dominating possession, constant movement and a defence that often takes on individual duels. The full-backs can advance into midfield and the forwards take part in the press. It is an aggressive model, capable of suffocating opponents, but one that also leaves space when the first line is beaten.

The impact of each at Real Madrid in 2026-27.

Direct involvements = goals + assists. In the Champions League, Vinicius played four games without a goal or an assist; Espi scored one goal in four games, against Roma. Points gained assume that, without Espi's goals, the three games would have ended in draws. Data up to 21 November 2026.

Sources: FotMob (Opta data), AS and TheStatsAPI.

Real Madrid have the tools to exploit these gaps. Vinicius and Mbappe can attack the space in behind, while Bellingham and Guler have the ability to receive between the lines and speed up the transition. The difficulty will be doing so without turning the game into a series of attacks and counter-attacks.

According to recent reports, real Madrid won their first four league-phase games in the Champions League and are second, with 12 points. The positive run brings calm, but it does not remove the need to improve the collective performance.

It has been revealed that mourinho already has an answer to one of the questions: Vinicius will start. He also knows what Espi can offer and why he does not intend simply to put him alongside Mbappe. The bigger challenge is to make Real Madrid take advantage of the quality of their attackers without losing control of midfield.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Keith Andrews said his decision to make several changes to Brentford's starting line-up against Everton on Monday revealed ambition to compete on all fronts this season.
  • Andrews watched on as his Brentford side responded from their 2-0 defeat to Brighton ahead of the international break with a thumping 4-0 triumph over 10-man Everton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Keith Andrews said his decision to make several changes to Brentford's starting line-up against Everton on Monday revealed ambition to compete on all fronts this season.

Andrews watched on as his Brentford side responded from their 2-0 defeat to Brighton ahead of the international break with a thumping 4-0 triumph over 10-man Everton.

Keane Lewis-Potter netted twice in the space of 178 seconds in the first half to put the Bees in control before Everton captain James Tarkowski was sent off in the 40th minute.

Tarkowski was dismissed for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk high on his shin after clearing the ball, with referee Craig Pawson overruling his original decision after a VAR review.

Vitaly Janelt's 67th-minute thunderbolt was the pick of Brentford's goals, with substitute Fabio Carvalho climbing off the bench to add further gloss to the scoreline late on.

Brentford enjoyed their joint-biggest home win in the Premier League, equalling their 4-0 rout of Manchester United in August 2022, with their display coming after Andrews elected to make four changes to the side that were beaten by Brighton.

Callum Wilson replaced the suspended Igor Thiago up front, while Yarmoliuk, Mikkel Damsgaard and Jaidon Anthony all came in to replace Mamadou Sangare and Kevin Schade, while Aaron Hickey missed out all together through injury.

It has been revealed that "Major impact, it's the nature of the game and the squad. We have the luxury of choosing from very good players," Andrews told Sky Sports on the reason behind his alterations.

"Some will be disappointed not to play more, but the reality is we need everybody. We want to be ambitious, so we need everybody. The boys that came in did really well.".

— Everton (@Everton) November 23, 2026.

After missing out on European football last season, Brentford's win saw them climb up to sixth in the Premier League and just four points adrift of fourth-place Liverpool.

"We know what the other side feels like, but I wanted to keep our habits, be professional, try to control the game and wait for the right openings," Andrews added.

It has been revealed that "Each game is very different, very difficult. The expectation levels at this club have changed and, regardless of the performance, the win to go sixth in the league and still questions about 'should they be doing better?' – I think people need to get real.

It has been revealed that "I'm really happy with the group, the club and long may it continue. Long way to go. Onto Old Trafford on Saturday and we're really looking forward to it.".

Since Andrews took charge of Brentford ahead of the 2025-26 season, of London clubs, only Arsenal (113) have won more Premier League points than the Bees (70).

Brentford also hit the 300-goal mark in the Premier League in their 201st game in the competition (303 goals in total), the fifth-fastest side to do so, after Man United (165), Newcastle United (170), Liverpool (190) and Blackburn Rovers (191).

Lewis-Potter got the landmark goal, and in 11 appearances this season, he has already beaten his best-ever scoring season in the Premier League (three in 36 apps in 2025-26 and 3 in 30 in 2023-24), with his double taking him to four this term.

"He's been excellent, growing all the time since I've been here," Andrews stated of Lewis-Potter.

"Finds himself in unnatural positions – we give him the freedom to go and roam, and he's proving very difficult for the opposition to mark.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup will be hosted jointly by England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, FIFA have confirmed, with the tournament returning to the United Kingdom for the first time since 1966.

The UK was the sole bidder to host the tournament, and received a 4.3 out of 5 rating from FIFA evaluators.

In a recent development, the bid has put forward 19 potential venues, including five in London: Wembley Stadium, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Emirates, Stamford Bridge and a renovated Selhurst Park. Old Trafford will be considered, regardless of whether Manchester United moves to its proposed new home.

According to recent reports, some 32 teams will contest the 2027 World Cup in Brazil, but this is due to expand to 48 from 2031 onwards. The tournament, then, will comprise 104 matches.

England has not hosted a major tournament since staging the women’s European Championships in 2022, which the Lionesses won. It has failed in bids to host the 2006 and 2018 men’s World Cups. England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the Men’s European Championship in 2028.

It is understood that the process of finalising the list of stadia that will be used is ongoing and is under FIFA’s jurisdiction. Wembley is the only stadium that currently meets the standards required to host the World Cup final.

It is still to be decided how many of the co-host nations will qualify automatically for the tournament.

The 2035 World Cup bid has also put forward a host stadium in Northern Ireland - Belfast’s Windsor Park - and two each in Scotland and Wales. The Scottish grounds are Glasgow’s Hampden Park and Edinburgh’s Easter Road, while the Welsh pair are both in Cardiff: the Millennium Stadium and the Cardiff City Stadium.

The remaining English host stadiums are: Villa Park, The AmEx, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, and the Stadium of Light.

Three more stadia could be added to the bid, most notably a potential newly introduced Chelsea ground. Discussions as to the future of Stamford Bridge have been bubbling away for decades as the club’s hierarchy debate whether to redevelop the current ground, knock it down to build a new one on the current site, or move to a new site altogether.

Birmingham City’s new Powerhouse Stadium and Wrexham’s renovated Racecourse Ground could also host matches.

According to recent reports, prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed the news, saying: “The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women’s sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.

“Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep - and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle.”.

FA CEO Mark Bullingham noted: “Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play. Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations.”.

In a recent development, england last hosted a World Cup in 1966, when the men’s team famously beat West Germany 4-2 in the final to seal the nation’s first major honour. The Lionesses have since become back-to-back Euros champions in 2022 and 2025, but suffered World Cup final heartbreak in 2023 when they were beaten 1-0 by Spain in Sydney.

Before the UK’s host bid for 2035 was confirmed at a special FIFA Congress, it was also revealed that a joint bid by the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica had been approved to host the 2031 World Cup.

The Argentine endured a horror start to his tenure at Old Trafford with a heavy 4-0 defeat by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

The Red Devils were down to ten men inside eight minutes when Leny Yoro was sent off for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity.

United suffered no injury blows on Merseyside, but the result was “painful” according to their new head coach, and he will be looking to put things right immediately in Europe’s top competition on Wednesday.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss sprung a surprise with his inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in his starting XI at Anfield, with the Dutchman having been sidelined for over a year with a persistent back injury.

The centre-half looked awkward for much of the match, and his selection was scrutinised intensely afterwards.

It remains to be seen whether he will play again here, with Harry Maguire introduced in the first half and shoring up United’s back five.

The England international should start here, perhaps alongisde Yoro, who will not be suspended for this match with his ban only for league games.

That could see Lisandro Martinez plugged at left-back once more, although the Argentine had to shift back inside after Yoro’s red card, with Dorgu shifting back to wing-back from his left wing berth.

Diogo Dalot failed to truly impress on Merseyside and could see himself rotated for Noussair Mazraoui, while in the engine room, Youri Tielemans was hooked for Mason Mount in the second half.

Bryan Mbeumo was the man sacrificed following the sending-off as Pochettino resorted to damage limitation, but the Cameroon international should get the nod here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 13:30, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 10:05.

Barcelona will aim to make it five straight wins in all competitions when they continue their Champions League campaign away to Sabah on Wednesday night.

History will be made in this contest, as the two teams prepare to lock horns for the first time, and it would be one of the biggest shocks in Champions League history should Sabah manage to overcome the La Liga champions.

Sabah boast a record of one win and three draws from their four matches in this season's Champions League league phase, which has left them in 31st spot in the table on three points, one point behind 24th-placed PSV Eindhoven.

The Owls opened their league stage campaign with a 4-0 loss to Manchester United, before managing to record a 2-0 victory over Slavia Prague in their second fixture to put three points on the board, but they have since lost to Borussia Dortmund and Viking FC.

Valdas Dambrauskas's side will enter this match off the back of a huge domestic win, beating Sumqayit 5-1, with the result leaving them third in Azerbaijan's top flight, picking up 24 points from their opening 11 games of the season.

Including qualification matches, Sabah have a record of seven wins and five losses in this season's Champions League, keeping five clean sheets in the process.

The Owls had never played in the European Cup before this season, so it is a historic campaign for the club, and they will take on Villarreal, Napoli and Arsenal in their three Champions League league stage fixtures after this one.

As for Barcelona, the Catalan side are right now fifth in the league phase table, picking up nine points from their four matches courtesy of a record of three wins and one defeat.

Hansi Flick's side beat Feyenoord and Galatasaray in their opening two league stage fixtures before suffering a 4-2 reverse to Paris Saint-Germain, but they managed to post a 3-0 victory over Aston Villa last time out to get back on track.

Barcelona will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 win over Villarreal, with that result moving them back to the top of the La Liga table, three points ahead of Real Madrid.

The Catalan side lost in the last-16 stage of last season's Champions League to Atletico Madrid, and it remains to be seen whether their defensive unit is strong enough to make a serious challenge for the 2026-27 European Cup.

Barcelona have actually conceded in each of their last 12 away group stage/league phase matches, but they have scored at least twice in 17 of their last 19 games at this point.

Barcelona Champions League form:.

Barcelona form (all competitions):.

Sabah will be without the services of Aden McCarthy, with the centre-back suspended on Wednesday following his red card in the team's last Champions League match with Viking.

The hosts also need to make a check on the fitness of Veljko Simic, who is struggling with an injury; the attacker has eight goals in 18 appearances this season and his absence would therefore be a major blow for Sabah.

Joy-Lance Mickels has been in impressive form this season, scoring 12 goals in 22 appearances, and the forward is set to start for the home team.

As for Barcelona, Lamine Yamal will not be involved due to a slight ankle problem, with Barcelona not prepared to take any risks when it comes to the Spain international.

Roony Bardghji (knee), Xavi Espart (ankle), Rodri (hamstring) and Andreas Christensen (muscle) are also unavailable for selection.

Pau Cubarsi did not play against Villarreal on Sunday due to an glitch that he sustained while on international duty with Spain, but the centre-back was on the bench and should feature in the starting team.

Meanwhile, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi are expected to join Raphinha in the final third of the field due to the absence of Yamal.

Sabah possible starting lineup:.

Pokatilov; Zedadka, Solvet, Almeida, Puchaz; Lepinjica, Isayev, Rakhomaliev; Severina, Mbina, Mickels.

Barcelona possible starting lineup:.

J Garcia; E Garcia, Cubarsi, Martin, Cancelo; Fermin, Bernal, Pedri; Adeyemi, Raphinha, Gordon.

Yamal's absence is a major blow for Barcelona, but the Catalan outfit have enough quality in their side to secure all three points on Wednesday.

Bruno Guimaraes revealed he apologised to the Arsenal squad after joining the club in the summer.

The Brazilian spent five years at Newcastle before completing a £75million move to Arsenal in August.

During his time on Tyneside, Guimaraes had several heated clashed with Arsenal’s midfielders, including Jorginho and Declan Rice.

Once he had switched loyalties and become a Gunner, the No39 addressed those battles with his newly introduced team-mates.

“I remember the first time I had to speak in front of everyone, the first thing I said was sorry to the boys.” Guimaraes said.

Sources indicate that “Because definitely, [those] who knows me know how much I hate to lose. I always play hard and I know I have some fights against them.

“So I say sorry now [we’re] in the same team, ‘I can’t wait to compete for you guys’.”.

It has been a patchy start to life at Arsenal for Guimaraes, who has had his best moments off the bench as a substitute.

He has struggled more when starting and his partnership with Rice has not looked a particularly balanced or natural one.

However, the 29-year-old insisted there is still “much more” to come from him, and he is determined to play his part in an Arsenal side challenging on all fronts.

“We push each other to always be playing well, because if you don’t play well, other players will come and play well,” Guimaraes said.

Industry observers note that “I think that’s very important for Arsenal. We want to make a dynasty here; we want to win everything possible. I think since I came to the club, the first thing Mikel said to me was create a dynasty for the club, so we want to win everything that’s possible.

Sources indicate that “I know how much the Champions League means for the fans, and for us here. Tomorrow we have a major test with a top team, they have been unbelievable this season, so tomorrow we have to play a very good game because it’s going to be against a top side.”.

Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha has revealed that he was “robbed” following Saturday’s Premier League match against Leeds.

Sources indicate that sources close to the Dutchman say that while his phone was not among the possessions stolen, personal belongings and several work-related items were taken. The incident took place outside a hotel in Mayfair on Saturday night.

Emegha was unhurt, with Chelsea understood to be aware of the situation and providing their full support to the player.

The Metropolitan Police are also aware of the situation.

Emegha scored against Leeds on what was his first Premier League start for Chelsea since arriving from BlueCo sister club Strasbourg in the summer, but his goal made little difference in the end as Leeds won 4-1 against Xabi Alonso’s side.

The 23-year-old took to Instagram on Sunday evening to reveal that he had been robbed in London shortly after the match.

“Unfortunately after the game I was robbed,” Emegha wrote. “I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.”.

The post started: “First goal, disappointing result, we’ll be back stronger on Friday [against Nottingham Forest].”.

Emegha’s transfer to Chelsea was agreed in September 2025 but he remained at Strasbourg last season and arrived at Stamford Bridge in the summer.

He scored 31 goals in 78 total appearances for Strasbourg across all competitions and opened his account for Chelsea on his third outing.

After nursing a hamstring injury at the beginning of the season, he made his first competitive appearance off the bench in Chelsea’s Carabao Cup last-16 defeat by Liverpool last month before then being handed a league debut in the 1-0 loss at Sunderland before the international break.

As far as auditions to replace Cristiano Ronaldo go, Carlos Forbs' couldn't have gone much better.

His winner against Wales on Tuesday certainly looked and felt like a Ronaldo goal, especially from early in the former Manchester United star's career.

Recent findings suggest that right flank. Dribbling at pace. Ben Davies back-tracking. A quick flap inside with the left boot. Shoot. Goal. He only needed 11 minutes since coming on to change the game - and potentially his career trajectory.

Portugal's No7 later insisted he did not feel the 'weight' of the shirt, but the jersey is pregnant with meaning. Ronaldo wore No 7 for the national team for 20 years, inheriting it from the legendary Luis Figo. Its next permanent incumbent matters deeply in the Portuguese footballing psyche.

Sources indicate that forbs has not inherited it full-time yet, as a source within the Portugal camp has confirmed to Daily Mail Sport. He appears locked in a battle with Rafael Leao, who was supposed to have it this international break until he missed out through injury.

But now Forbs - a chap who went to school in Leeds and was praised by Erling Haaland while at Manchester City - is the name on fans' lips.

Carlos Forbs is gunning to be Portugal's latest full-time No7 after Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement - and his audition against Wales went swimmingly.

Ronaldo held the shirt for 20 years, having inherited it from the legendary Luis Figo.

Industry observers note that they are already calling him 'CF7' and media outlets across the world hailed the 22-year-old, a relative unknown for plays for Club Brugge. 'The fresh national hero,' is how leading Portuguese outlet O Jogo described him. No pressure, kid.

It has been revealed that his form is attracting attention on British shores. Rangers were interested in him over the summer, as were Lyon. Daily Mail Sport has been unable to verify recent reports that the likes of Arsenal, Aston Villa, Everton and Newcastle are keen.

According to recent reports, but it would be no surprise to see him in the Premier League one day. Stardom has long felt like it might be on the cards for Forbs. Born in Sintra to Bissau-Guinean parents, he started off playing futsal and was picked up by Sporting Lisbon's academy, just like Ronaldo. His family left for England when he was just 11, and it wasn't long before Manchester City came calling.

In a recent development, the attacker spent eight years in the City academy and was considered a gem. In 2022-23 he was named Premier League 2 player of the season after a stunning campaign which saw him score 29 goals and provide 18 assists in all competitions.

He had a knack of scoring hat-tricks - not a bad habit to adopt. In one match he scored four against Manchester United like it was child's play. It felt like nothing could go wrong for the winger, who copied Ronaldo's lesser-known 'nap' celebration to mock the Red Devils. A player who looked up to the likes of Raheem Sterling and Phil Foden didn't look far off joining them in the first team.

It has been revealed that he was rewarded with chances to train alongside Pep Guardiola's seniors, and Kyle Walker and Bernardo Silva were noted as being particularly welcoming. Erling Haaland was impressed with him. Watching a montage including the youngster's goals, he remarked: 'Is that Carlos? I've been training a lot with these guys. Carlos is good.'.

But a debut never came due to the competition at City and in 2023, yearning for opportunities to play in the big-time, he moved to Ajax in a £17million deal.

'I didn’t have to leave, but in the summer, clubs came along where I knew I had more prospects,' he told AD in October 2023, while he was still known as Carlos Borges.

Forbs, previously known as Carlos Borges, was a gem in Manchester City's academy but never got a first-team debut.

He was shipped off to Ajax but struggled to nail down a starter spot and was harshly cast aside.

It has been revealed that 'The media made me big, but I didn’t really feel like I was getting many opportunities in Manchester. I didn’t know if that would change this season. Of course, I already knew that Ajax focuses on youth. When I heard the aims, I thought OK, I want to try my luck at this club.

Industry observers note that 'A number of staff members at Manchester City also wanted to see me make the final step after ten years. Me too, at the club where I grew up, just as it was my parents’ dream. But I concluded that it was even better to take this opportunity.'.

But things didn't work out for Forbs in the Netherlands. Playing for such a dominant side against low blocks did not suit his electric pace and direct dribbling, even though he had managed at Manchester City, who had a similar philosophy.

He was a bit-part player in his first season and, in his second, was sent on loan to Wolves, where he had little impact in 10 Premier League appearances. While he had more game time under Gary O'Neil, he did not fit into Vitor Pereira's 3-4-2-1 system, which favoured wing-backs, when the Portuguese replaced the Englishman.

According to recent reports, by the summer of 2025, Ajax had seen enough, and dispensed of Forbs in brutal fashion. Technical director Alex Kroes informed seven players, including him, over WhatsApp that he was 'no longer welcome' at the club's training ground. Former Arsenal man Chuba Akpom was among them, too.

Industry observers note that if Forbs wanted to train, he had to wait until the first team were done. Even if it was a day of double sessions, he had to stay away until both were over. With three years remaining on his contract, his space in the car park had reportedly been removed. Access to the gym and canteen was only permitted when the first team were finished.

A once-dream move had soured within two years and he was cast away savagely, joining Belgian side Club Brugge - and that is where his career has been reborn.

Early into his Brugge career, in November 2025, he announced himself in Europe by scoring two goals and providing an assist against Barcelona in the Champions League.

Forbs has shone for Club Brugge and scored twice against Barcelona last season.

'Today is a dream come true,' he said after being awarded man of the match against Barca. It was the sort of night his youth coaches had known he was capable of.

After 10 goals in all competitions last season, he is already on five for this campaign and growing his reputation. He is on three Portugal caps now - he made his debut last year - and seems to have the trust of new manager Jorge Jesus.

In a recent development, when pressed if he was the latest permanent Portugal No7 on Tuesday, Forbs was coy. 'I try to do my best,' he stated.

Then he added: 'We know it's a big, blessed number and I hope to continue wearing this number and scoring many goals.'.

It has been revealed that it remains to be seen whether he will take on the mantle of Ronaldo, who scored a world record 146 goals for Portugal. The longer-term favourite is Leao, an established star who has won Serie A with AC Milan. But Leao has hit a rough patch in the last couple of years and as his stock wanes, Forbs' star is only rising.

Recent findings suggest that how happy is he? Is he satisfied?

Can you dream of winning the Scudetto?

Marking their return from November’s international break with a nightmare 4-1 drumming at home against historic rivals Leeds on Saturday, the Stamford Bridge support have made their frustrations abundantly clear.

Tumbling down the Premier League standings, Chelsea have now lost four of their previous five appearances across all competitions on either side of November’s fortnight interval.

Alonso officially put pen to paper on a four-year deal in SW6 back in May and remarkably became the third permanent manager in west London in the space of a calendar year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith.

Sources indicate that I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

There is no defending Chelsea, because again there was simply no defending by Chelsea.

One goal up and with home advantage against a Leeds team they had already beaten at Stamford Bridge this season in the Carabao Cup, Xabi Alonso and his players took that encouraging platform for success and ripped it up, deservedly losing 4-1.

At least Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United could play the “we only had 10 men” card.

Whatever is failing to function right now at Chelsea is a complex web spun by poor decision-making and performances from a whole host of implicated parties.

The Chelsea defence showcases the Blues’ endemic struggles for consistency in a perfect microcosmic form, not least because there are so many stakeholders who must each accept their share of the blame.

An injury record peculiarly problematic for a team largely only playing once a week this season in the absence of any European football has left them without captain Reece James, summer signing Maxence Lacroix and the improved Jorrel Hato - players whose availability might not cure all their defensive ills, but would certainly help.

Their absences mean more minutes for players not showing any signs that they possess the composure or robustness needed to provide support for a potent attack and secure a return to the Champions League.

Malo Gusto was beaten twice for Brenden Aaronson’s run to goal for Leeds’ fourth - something that happens all too often for a player valued by Chelsea at £75million in the summer transfer market.

Wesley Fofana remains a liability, and his £75m transfer fee back in 2022 - £89.2m adjusted for inflation - surely makes him the worst pound-for-pound signing Chelsea have made in the BlueCo era.

And while Josh Acheampong, 20, has been the one Chelsea defender to draw consistent praise in the first three months of the campaign, he was suspect against Leeds.

So too was Levi Colwill, a player with enormous potential but who has so far failed to rediscover his physicality and form since the torn anterior cruciate ligament that kept him sidelined for almost all of last season.

A question it is worth Alonso and his coaching staff asking themselves: is 34-year-old Emi Martinez clearly a better goalkeeper than Mike Penders, the inevitable long-term No1?

Fresh details emerge as Chelsea star ‘robbed’ after Leeds game.

Transfer news LIVE: Shock Arsenal move; Man Utd striker deal.

Chelsea get fresh Rogers penalty review after Leeds handball controversy.

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events.

There is a case to be made to fully blood Penders now, whatever promises might have been made to Martinez when he joined. The Argentine currently looks a shadow of the commanding player he was at Aston Villa.

Wesley Fofana must surely be Chelsea’s worst pound-for-pound signing in the BlueCo era.

Individual errors from Fofana and Gusto and the softness of Colwill and Martinez mean plenty of the blame is rightly being portioned in their direction, but other parties are just as culpable.

Alonso, for example, has flattered to deceive as manager so far, switching between a back three and a back four with the result that his team look capable of playing neither, not both. His Chelsea side have scored a laudable 20 league goals but conceded a lamentable 20 at the other end.

Recent findings suggest that responsibility also lies at the boardroom door, where questionable recruitment has taken place. Benoit Badiashile and Axel Disasi were not at the standard required and have taken too long to move on (still neither player has permanently left the club).

And while he is far from the complete product, Trevoh Chalobah had been one of the more consistent centre-backs of the Clearlake era yet was moved on to high-flying Como this summer in favour of handing a greater amount of game time to Fofana.

If Chelsea are to get back to the pinnacle of English football, which is where the club sees itself, then recruitment, coaching and player performances must all improve.

Accepting shared responsibility is the first step towards revamping and properly rebuilding a defence that simply isn’t going to deliver Champions League football on current form.

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

England always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the new half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.

Recent findings suggest that will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

According to recent reports, having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the big delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon stated of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”.

Sources indicate that A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

Industry observers note that as for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

“Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel remarked. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

Industry observers note that czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL.

Industry observers note that england had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Sources indicate that even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

Recent findings suggest that “I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold noted later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”.

When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon remarked, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

“If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel stated when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against Newly introduced Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

“I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

Recent findings suggest that “But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”.

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

The Professional Footballers’ Association has leapt to Cole Palmer’s defence following his withdrawal from the England squad.

The union’s CEO,  Maheta Molango, noted the Chelsea forward is a victim of a “sick” system that is demanding too much from players physically.

“When England see five players who need to withdraw when the single most proud moment a player has is to be called up for the national team, you just ask yourself, what’s wrong about the industry?” Molango said at the Fifpro performance summit in London.

“You see people like Cole Palmer, someone who would have played four consecutive summers in a row had he gone to the World Cup, and you wonder why is he missing?”He’s missing because he’s a victim of the calendar and that’s something that needs to absolutely trigger the alarm bells.”.

Trevoh Chalobah will earn his third England cap in tonight’s Nations League match against Czech Republic. The Como centre-back, 27, played in the 6-4 defeat of France in the Bronze final at the World Cup and his other appearance for the Three Lions was in the defeat by Senegal last year.

Trent Alexander-Arnold will make his first England appearance in 15 months after being given a start. The Real Madrid full-back, who was not selected for the World Cup in the summer, earned his last cap against Andorra in 2025.

He replaces Jarell Quansah in Thomas Tuchel’s line-up that lost to Spain at the weekend.

“Trent had a very good training week and the excellent training in Wembley after the match, where he showed that he absolutely wants to play and wants to be with us,” said Tuchel on the eve of the game at Fortuna Arena.

“We’re good. Everything is fine. He’s ready to go. He has qualities that you all know, like he’s strong on the ball, excellent crossing, good finishing. And very, very good on the ball. That’s basically what he brings.”.

Ezri Konsa, who missed team training on the day before this game, is out. Morgan Rogers, meanwhile, steps in for Jude Bellingham in the No10 role as Tuchel looks to juggle four matches in 11 days during this extended international break.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is in line to make his first England start under head coach Thomas Tuchel for tonight’s Nations League game against Czech Republic.

Injuries to Nico O’Reilly and Ezri Konsa have forced Tuchel into changes at the back, with Alexander-Arnold expected to come in at right-back, Trevoh Chalobah to replace Konsa and Lewis Hall to step in for O’Reilly.

Industry observers note that alexander-Arnold has made only one appearance under Tuchel, as a substitute in a World Cup qualifying win against Andorra in June 2025. His last start for England came under interim head coach Lee Carsley, when he scored in a victory over Finland.

Jude Belllingham could be given a rest after playing the full 90 minutes in the defeat by Spain, which would give Morgan Rogers an opportunity in the No 10 position.

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme.

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Uefa Nations League match between Czech Republic and England from Slavia Prague’s Eden Stadium. The home side, 49th in the Fifa rankings, scrambled their way to World Cup qualification with victories in the play-offs in penalty shoot-outs over Ireland and Denmark, promptly stank Group A out in Mexico/Canada/United States, drawing with South Africa but losing to South Korea and Mexico to finish last.

Sources indicate that miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

Santi started his stint in charge and this campaign in Group A3 with a 2-1 defeat by Croatia but there were some very positive signs – they set up as a 4-3-3 in classic Spanish/Cruyff style and pressed like dervishes. England, who conceded three goals when players made mistakes when subjected to aggressive pressing in their opening 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain, will have to find better solutions tonight, either by holding their nerve or counterpressing with fewer mistakes.

Given England are ranked 45 places higher, their results, if not all performances, at the World Cup were commendable and the way in which they rattled Spain and should really have given themselves a bulwark against the comeback by converting their penalty at 2-1 up,  an away win should be relatively straightforward. But they did lose on their last visit to Prague in a Euro 2020 qualifier having won 5-0 in the home leg.

Fernandes is not ready to commit just yet, leaving his options open for now after Mauricio Pochettino arrived this week to replace Michael Carrick as manager.

These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine.

Mudryk has won 28 caps for Ukraine but is yet to represent them since his ban was overturned.

In a recent development, 'The UAF completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk's representatives with the information they requested and remained in contact with those working on the case.

Towards the end of last season, Jeltsch got his hands on his first piece of silverware at club level as Stuttgart got the better of Arminia Bielefel to win the German Cup for the first time in 28 years.

Liverpool are also being credited with a strong interest in a hotly contested race which will only become more competitive if Jeltsch continues on the same meteoric trajectory.

It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Sources indicate that russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

In a recent development, toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian mentioned. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

Recent findings suggest that “It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.
